pillar_reactions.evidence: "Yeah, 100%" to the approach, and he immediately volunteered which part mattered most to him and why: "the last thing you said, it's also very important to me. You know, if it's a program of six months, after those six months, I don't want to be back to square one. I want to be able to continue, have the tools to continue with the training by myself." He had already pre-sold himself on the mechanism before the call — "it just made total sense, like more mobile, more intensity, less time at the gym, just a kettlebell".

Agreement with a mild deflection rather than resistance: "yeah, it does make sense. As you probably said, nutrition wise, I feel the least, I don't feel weak nutrition wise." He made his own case (farm produce, nothing processed) and then conceded the point — "obviously open to suggestions" — and closed on "as long as I know we're on the same page, but as long as it's nothing processed food, I'm happy." The pillar was the shortest of the three and the rep effectively conceded it was already handled.

First answer was "No, it sounds good. No, no, no questions", then he corrected himself and asked a sequence of mechanics questions: "So in the app, I will get like the 30 to 40 minute training that I have to do for that day of the week... And is it going to be like a video or like written?" followed by how to choose a kettlebell and whether one is enough. All practical, none resistant.

anchors.raw: to be honest, it's a high investment for me. I always expect, I'm just completely honest, I was expecting a bit less
anchors.note: A pure expectation anchor with no competitor attached — he had formed a number in his head from Trevor's free content and the setter call and $6,000 exceeded it. Worth knowing what the setter conveys about price, since the anchor was already set before the closer arrived.

anchors.raw: I got two horses and you have no idea how much a horse is expensive on a daily, on a monthly basis... vets are way more expensive than this program.
anchors.note: Two horses consume essentially his entire monthly surplus, which is the mechanical reason a payment plan could not work. The interesting detail is that he volunteered the favourable comparison himself — vet bills exceed the programme cost — and the rep agreed about horses being expensive rather than picking the comparison up. A prospect making your value argument for you is not a common gift.

anchors.raw: about four years, five years ago, I did one year of work with a personal trainer and we did one year of rings
anchors.note: He has previously paid a personal trainer for a full year and stopped only because that trainer moved abroad, not because of cost or dissatisfaction — "they were a lot of fun". A precedent for sustained coaching spend that was never priced or used.

anchors.raw: even not even training outside. My garden with a kettlebell for 45 minutes, instead of going one hour and a half at the gym, plus 15 minutes, both ways, back and forth, it would help
anchors.note: He costed the incumbent in time himself — two hours per session against 45 minutes — and framed it as the reason the model appeals. Supportive and unused.

unmet_demand.want: Supervised coaching with form correction at a price he can actually reach
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is nothing between $6,000 for one-to-one coaching and $200 a month for a self-paced course with no form correction. He identified the gap himself the moment it was offered: "do you think it's still easy enough to learn by myself without someone correcting me? That's the question basically." For a prospect with a live back injury and no kettlebell experience, that gap is the whole decision.

unmet_demand.want: An explanation for three to four years of recurring minor injuries
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This is his most-felt problem — "That's why I would love to know, to have an answer for this. I have no idea. I've asked myself this question many times" — and nobody answered it. The rep offered two speculative causes, insufficient mobility work and a possible protein or B12 deficiency, without diagnosing either. The programme's mobility component plausibly addresses part of it and the case was never actually made.

unmet_demand.want: To defer the start until his back has recovered, without losing programme time
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered with "We can work around that. No worries" and no mechanism. Whether the six months can be paused or start-dated is not defined anywhere on the call, and the same question was answered differently on another call in this batch, where an injury mid-programme was said to pause and extend the term.
